rows.title: x402 on Celo mainnet: which tokens a smart account can actually pay in
rows.note: Measured by infra on a Celo mainnet fork, by installing an always-valid ERC-1271 contract and calling as it. USDC: EIP-3009 and permit, both accepting ERC-1271, so our wallets work. USD₮ and USA₮: neither surface exists. USDm, EURm, KESm: permit only, and ecrecover-only, so a contract wallet cannot sign one. The Mento local-currency tokens are signable by an EOA but not by a smart account, which excludes the whole agent category from exactly the tokens that make Celo interesting. Recommendation 1 of the standards audit

rows.title: x402 on Celo: what an agent can actually pay in
rows.status: Permit2 with local settlement, not EIP-3009
rows.note: Milestone finding. Celo USDC is FiatTokenV2 and does expose the EIP-3009 surface (version() = "2", authorizationState answers), but it verifies the authorization with ecrecover, so an Altana smart account cannot produce a signature it accepts. Phrase it that way: "Celo USDC has no EIP-3009" would be wrong. Proven on a fork 2026-09-28: an EOA settles USDC over EIP-3009, an Altana account settles over permit2-exact with ERC-1271. Consistent with infra's mainnet audit, where USDC is the only token an agent can pay in

rows.title: The relay reserves no nonce: two intents prepared before the first mines collide
rows.status: Relay bug stands (N1); SDK survives it from PR #104
rows.note: Unchanged as a relay defect. SDK PR #104 adds a bounded retry: qa verified live that four back-to-back operations on one wallet now all confirm, where the same shape gave InvalidNonce and a failed grant on 2026-09-28. Correction to earlier guidance: "wait for the previous transaction to mine" is NOT sufficient — both of sdk's live failures came *after* a confirmed receipt, because the relay's read of latest lags the receipts it hands out. Also closed off: a client-supplied nonce is not a narrower fix but a broken one, since the sequence key changes at the delegation transition

rows.title: Cache proof: key valid in the Celo mirror, anchored L1 block
rows.note: A key is now live in the Celo mirror: proved through the test bench on 2026-09-29, isValidKey true, sourceBlockNumber 11807900 equal to the anchor, and keccak(cached publicKey) == keyId verified on chain. The deployed cache is KeyStoreCacheOPStack 1.1.1 and isValidKey requires sourceBlockNumber == IL1Block.number() — equality, not recency. So a cached key is an assertion about one anchored L1 block, true inside a window, not a durable mirror. qa measured the anchor live 2026-09-29: 11807636 against a Sepolia head of 11807722, 86 blocks / ~17 minutes behind, matching sdk's 70-95. Consequences: a KeyStore write is provable ~30 min after it lands, and a proof is good for ~20 min. My own fork-celo-cache run already showed the equality rule from the other side — moving the anchor one block made isCachedKeyValid go false. evidence/2026-09-29-celo-sepolia-anchor-lag.md

rows.title: Short timebox expires, then rejection
rows.status: Proven (live); fails on fork mode B for a fork-specific reason
rows.note: The timebox is proven live: a key granted with a 150s expiry executed, then the same key was rejected 14s past its expiry with nothing else changed. On fork mode B it fails deterministically, even in isolation — the relay reports the just-authorized key as unknown on the very next prepare. Not the nonce bug (it fails with nothing else in flight, and anvil's instant mining closes that window), and not a grant lying about success (the authorize tx emits Authorized; ruled out from the event log). Cause not fully established; a fork collapses the gap between a tx landing and the next request to zero. evidence/2026-09-28-s5b-fork-only-failure.md
